title: Characterization of Mirror Twin Boundaries in Monolayer MoS2 via Atomic Resolution STEM and 4D-STEM
content: Recent advances in aberration-corrected STEM and 4D-STEM, enabled by ultrafast direct electron detection (DED), have revolutionized atomic-scale characterization of materials. Here, we employ these techniques to investigate the mirror twin boundaries (MTBs) in intentionally synthesized monolayer MoS2 flakes with controlled antiparallel grain orientations (60o rotation) and embedded grain boundary pores. These deviations promote the formation of stabilizing four-membered ring (4-MR) and eight-membered ring (8-MR) pores at grain boundaries, facilitating stress release during synthesis. The well-defined eight-membered ring (8-MR) pores are formed at the boundaries and can serve as molecular sieves for efficient water-ion separation [1].
